newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 31.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Three executives of Columbia/HCA Healthcare were indicted on charges of defrauding the government.
* GOP Congressional leaders fixed a glitch in their capital-gains tax cut by setting a top rate of 28 percent on profits from the sale of securities held a year to 18 months.
* Apple co-founder Jobs turned down offers to lead the computer maker.
* Fujitsu agreed to buy the shares Amdahl its does not already own for $850 million.
* J.P. Morgan said it will acquire a 45 percent stake in American Century for about $900 million.
* UPS customers are preparing contingency plans as contract talks between the package delivery firm and the Teamsters approach a midnight strike deadline.
* The Dow Jones industrials jumped 80.36 to a record 8254.89.
* Several leading fund companies say July is proving to be one of the best months of the year.
* Several wireless phone firms plan to announce a venture that would allow them to jointly market a digital service in the U.S. and Canada under the brand name GSM alliance.
* New York State Electric rejected CalEnergy 's hostile $1.92 billion bid to buy the upstate utility.
* Small stock fraud is growing and the usual protections against so-called boiler-room operators are not working.
* MCI reported a quarterly net downturn of 6.7 percent.
* The FDA was ordered by a federal judge to withdraw approval of a generic drug, probably the first time a court has reversed such a decision.
* A booming economy has cut the government's borrowing.
* Some investors say they found a bargain in AMC Entertainment, where the CEO's health problems are stirring speculation about a takeover.
